newsitem.title: JAPAN: Crudes down in Asia on bearish API, wet trade calm.
newsitem.headline: Crudes down in Asia on bearish API, wet trade calm.

text.p: Crude oil prices were weak in late Asia on Wednesday, pressured mainly by weekly API data showing stock increases in crude and some products, traders said.
"The market's pretty quiet, and It's mostly API figures that's having an impact," one broker said.

The latest weekly API data showed increases in crude oil, gasoline and distillates for the week ended December 6. It showed that crude stocks climbed 324,000 barrels, distillate stocks rose by over two million barrels and gasoline was up by almost six million barrels.
January cash Brent was notionally assessed at $23.10/23.20.
The level was down some 20 cents from late U.S. trading levels.
In spreads February Brent/Dubai was notionally assessed at $1.80/1.90, compared with late U.S. trading levels of $1.85/1.90. March Brent/Dubai was notionally assessed at $1.85/1.95.

Wet trading was mostly light and quiet for both Gulf and regional crudes, traders said. There was unconfirmed talk that 600,000-barrels of a February Oman were sold to China at MPM plus 20 cents. Traders said less-than-anticipated availability of Masila might be supporting the Oman market.
There were vague rumours that a February Murban was done at ADNOC plus 70 cents, but details were unavailable.

In regional crudes, a January Minas was believed to have been offered at 50 cents above the official selling price. There were unconfirmed reports of possible January Minas deals done at a premium of 57-65 cents. A producer offered a January Tapis cargo at quotes plus $1.10. January paper Tapis was notionally assessed at around $24.
IOC has issued a tender to buy about one million barrels of February-loading crude oil including those from the Middle East, West Africa and Asia.
